newsitem.title: UK: ITALY 1997 SOFT WHEAT CROP DOWN AT 3.2 MLN T-HGCA.
newsitem.headline: ITALY 1997 SOFT WHEAT CROP DOWN AT 3.2 MLN T-HGCA.

text.p: Italian soft wheat output is set to fall by 16 percent to 3.2 million tonnes this year, according to the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority.
The lower crop results from a seven percent fall in the area planted and a 10 percent reduction in yields, following the spring drought, the HGCA said in its "Weekly Digest".
The reduction in area was mainly due to rain during the sowing season, along with low grain prices at planting time, which encouraged farmers to switch to oilseeds.
A likely drop in the durum wheat crop to 3.9 million tonnes from last year's 4.4 million was expected because of lower yields, the HGCA said.

Italy's reduced crop is good news for UK exporters. Lower milling wheat supplies meant that "Italian import requirements should rise significantly this year, which should help UK exports," the HGCA said.
